database.description: The name of the Spanner database the IAM binding applies to.
database.rationale: This is a required reference to the target database. It does not directly introduce a security risk but must be correctly configured to ensure IAM bindings are applied to the intended database.

instance.description: The name of the Spanner instance the database belongs to.
instance.rationale: This is a required reference to the parent Spanner instance. It does not directly introduce a security risk but must be correctly configured to ensure IAM bindings are applied to the intended instance.

member/members.description: Identities that will be granted the privilege in role. Can be allUsers, allAuthenticatedUsers, user, serviceAccount, group, or domain.
member/members.rationale: Granting access to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers makes the database publicly accessible, exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users. Only specific, trusted identities should be granted access.

role.description: The role that should be applied. Can be used per role with google_spanner_database_iam_binding.
role.rationale: The role determines the level of access granted to the members. Overly permissive roles such as roles/spanner.admin should be avoided in favour of least-privilege roles to reduce the attack surface.

policy_data.description: The policy data generated by a google_iam_policy data source.
policy_data.rationale: Policy data defines the full IAM policy for the resource. Misconfigured policy data can grant excessive permissions or expose the database to public access.

project.description: If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project field is optional and defaults to the provider project. It does not directly introduce a security risk but should be explicitly set to avoid applying IAM bindings to unintended projects.

condition.description: An IAM Condition for the binding.
condition.rationale: IAM conditions allow fine-grained access control. Without conditions, bindings apply unconditionally, which may grant broader access than intended.

expression.description: Textual representation of an expression in Common Expression Language syntax.
expression.rationale: The expression defines the condition logic. An incorrect or overly permissive expression can inadvertently grant broad access.

title.rationale: The title is a required label for the condition. It does not directly introduce a security risk but helps identify the purpose of the condition.

description.description: An optional description of the condition.
description.rationale: The description is an optional label for the condition. It does not directly introduce a security risk but helps document the purpose of the condition.
